territorial_scope.description: Creates a section of the Florida Statutes, applying to political advertisements and related communications in Florida.

evidence.quote: Section 1. Section 106.145, Florida Statutes, is created to read:

summary.short: From 1 July 2024, Florida requires political advertisements that use generative AI to depict a real person doing something that did not occur, made with intent to injure a candidate or deceive on a ballot issue, to carry a specified AI disclaimer. Omission is a first-degree misdemeanor.
summary.long: Section 1 creates s. 106.145, Florida Statutes, and defines generative artificial intelligence. Political advertisements, electioneering communications and other miscellaneous advertisements of a political nature must prominently state the disclaimer "Created in whole or in part with the use of generative artificial intelligence (AI)" where they contain generative AI content that appears to depict a real person performing an action that did not occur, created with intent to injure a candidate or deceive regarding a ballot issue. The disclaimer is additional to other chapter 106 disclaimers. Subsection (3) sets size, font and audibility requirements by medium. A person identified under another chapter 106 disclaimer as paying for, sponsoring or approving such an advertisement who omits the disclaimer commits a first-degree misdemeanor, in addition to civil penalties provided by law. Any person may file a complaint with the Florida Elections Commission under s. 106.25, and expedited hearings apply. Section 2 sets the effective date as July 1, 2024.

notes: The disclaimer duty in s. 106.145(2) applies only if all three conditions hold: generative AI content, depiction of a real person performing an action that did not occur, and creation with intent to injure a candidate or deceive regarding a ballot issue. The penalty in (4)(a) covers only a person identified under another chapter 106 disclaimer as paying for, sponsoring or approving the advertisement. Civil penalties are referred to only generally ('provided by law'); no civil penalty amount is stated. The document does not state the session law chapter number or the bill's legislative history. Section 1 of the act contains a stray page-number artifact ('66') within s. 106.145(4)(b).

thresholds.note: No numeric cutoff changes legal treatment in s. 106.145. The numbers present are display specifications for the disclaimer (12-point bold font in 3(a); 4 percent of picture or graphic height in 3(b) and 3(e); at least 3 seconds of audio in 3(d)). Under the codebook these belong in the disclaimer obligation, not in thresholds. Scope turns on conditions without numeric cutoffs (generated content depicting a real person, intent to injure or deceive). The July 1, 2024 effective date is an event, and the penalty tier is enforcement.
